title: Effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of exenatide

citation.title: Effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of exenatide

printed_heading.text: Effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of exenatide Helle Linnebjerg, Prajakti A. Kothare,1 Soomin Park,1 Kenneth Mace,1 Shobha Reddy,1 Malcolm Mitchell & Robert Lins2 Eli Lilly and Co., Lilly Research Centre, Windlesham, UK, 1 Eli Lilly and Co., Lilly Corporate Center, Indianapolis, IN, USA and 2 SGS Research Unit Stuivenberg, Antwerp, Belgium OnlineOpen:This article is available free online at www.blackwell-synergy.com What is already known about this subject • Nonclinical studies have shown that exenatide is primarily cleared by the renal system. • It was not known to what degree the clinical pharmacokinetics and tolerability would be affected by increasing renal impairment (RI). What this study adds • Patients with mild to moderate RI adequately tolerate current therapeutic doses of exenatide. • However, exenatide is not recommended in patients with severe RI or end-stage renal disease. Correspondence Helle Linnebjerg PhD, Lilly Research Centre, Eli Lilly and Company, Erl Wood Manor, Sunninghill Road, Windlesham, Surrey GU20 6PH, UK. Tel: + 44 12 7648 3577 Fax: + 44 12 7648 3416 E-mail: linnebjerg_helle@lilly.com ............................................................................................................................. Keywords end-stage renal disease, exenatide, incretin mimetic, pharmacokinetics, renal impairment, Type 2 diabetes ............................................................................................................................. Received 15 November 2005 Accepted 6 January 2007 Published OnlineEarly 10 April 2007 Aims To evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK), safety and tolerability of a single exenatide dose in patients with renal impairment (RI). Methods Exenatide (5 or 10 mg) was injected subcutaneously in 31 subjects (one with Type 2 diabetes) stratified by renal function [Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance (CrCL), number of subjects]: normal (>80 ml min-1 , n = 8), mild RI (51–80 ml min-1 , n = 8), moderate RI (31–50 ml min-1 , n = 7) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring haemodialysis (n = 8). PK data were combined with four previous single-dose studies in patients with Type 2 diabetes to explore the relationship of exenatide clearance (CLp/F) and CrCL. Results Mean half-life for healthy, mild RI, moderate RI and ESRD groups were 1.5, 2.1, 3.2 and 6.0 h, respectively. endpoint.text: Exenatide plasma concentrations were evaluated by standard noncompartmental methods to determine key pharmacokinetic parameters.
The effects of dialysis in patients with ESRD were to be evaluated in this study by measuring plasma exenatide concentrations before (48 h postdose) and after a dialysis cycle.
Furthermore, the relationship between exenatide clearance and creatinine clearance was evaluated by fitting a linear mixed-effects model.

reported_results.text: For the ESRD group, the clearance was approximately one-quarter of the healthy control group (P < 0.001) and dose–weight normalized AUC0–α and Cmax were 3.37 (P < 0.001) and 1.38 Br J Clin Pharmacol
Mean exenatide clearance (CLp/F) was substantially reduced in subjects with ESRD (0.9 l h-1) compared with the control group (3.4 l h-1).

Results of the combined analysis showed that exenatide clearance was not significantly different between the normal renal function and mild renal impairment groups (P = 0.26), but was significantly reduced by 36% in the moderate renal impairment group (P = 0.008) and 84% in the ESRD group (P < 0.001) compared with the normal control group (Table 5).

In these results, patients with moderate RI had an AUC 1.63 times that of the control group (P = 0.003) and patients with ESRD had an increase in AUC 6.24 times that of the control group (P < 0.001).

However, interpolation from a linear fit of exenatide clearance vs. creatinine clearance for patients with severe RI showed a relatively low mean exenatide clearance of 1.82–3.03 l h-1 for this subgroup.

numbers.text: Study ‘D’ was a randomized, open-label, single-dose crossover study using 10 μg exenatide.

Each subject in this group received a single subcutaneous dose of 10 μg exenatide and safety and tolerability data from at least three subjects were evaluated prior to the dosing of subjects with moderate RI.

Methods Exenatide (5 or 10 μg) was injected subcutaneously in 31 subjects (one with Type 2 diabetes) stratified by renal function [Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance (CrCL), number of subjects]: normal (>80 ml min-1, n = 8), mild RI (51–80 ml min-1, n = 8), moderate RI (31–50 ml min-1, n = 7) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring haemodialysis (n = 8).

The effects of dialysis in patients with ESRD were to be evaluated in this study by measuring plasma exenatide concentrations before (48 h postdose) and after a dialysis cycle.
For the ESRD group, the clearance was approximately one-quarter of the healthy control group (P < 0.001) and dose–weight normalized AUC0–α and Cmax were 3.37 (P < 0.001) and 1.38 Br J Clin Pharmacol
Mean exenatide clearance (CLp/F) was substantially reduced in subjects with ESRD (0.9 l h-1) compared with the control group (3.4 l h-1).

Results of the combined analysis showed that exenatide clearance was not significantly different between the normal renal function and mild renal impairment groups (P = 0.26), but was significantly reduced by 36% in the moderate renal impairment group (P = 0.008) and 84% in the ESRD group (P < 0.001) compared with the normal control group (Table 5).

In these results, patients with moderate RI had an AUC 1.63 times that of the control group (P = 0.003) and patients with ESRD had an increase in AUC 6.24 times that of the control group (P < 0.001).

However, interpolation from a linear fit of exenatide clearance vs. creatinine clearance for patients with severe RI showed a relatively low mean exenatide clearance of 1.82–3.03 l h-1 for this subgroup.
In this study, a single 5- or 10-μg subcutaneous dose of exenatide appeared generally well tolerated in all evaluated stages of renal function except the ESRD group.
